basis: Item 0: three Q3 deliverables (Delivery Plan, mining contract, SFA drawdown) still outstanding; either they land in the window or the annual report shows a slip, and the two branches roughly cancel.
against: Silver drives this name day to day, and a Plan release inside the window would easily swamp any slip read; the sign is a coin flip.

basis: Item 0: underground mined grades of 2.7-3.4 g/t against a 5.0 g/t reserve point to a weaker underground reserve in the statement due end of September, partly offset by open-pit additions at a higher price deck.
against: Reserve days have been bought twice, open-pit additions at a higher gold price may net to growth, and the statement may not fall inside the window at all.

basis: Item 0: 183.6m placement shares (about 13% of the register) issued at A$0.305 begin trading on 28 Sep with spot already below the issue price, so underwater placees could sell into the window.
against: The timetable is public and the stock already trades below the issue price, and long-only resources funds rarely flip, so the supply may already be absorbed.

basis: Items 0 and 3: holding the 202.8p FY consensus needs an 80/20 H2 skew off a 38-42p H1, and the dividend policy implies about 1.1x interim cover, both of which the outlook paragraph has to address.
against: H1 was pre-announced in July and September interims after a July update have moved only -4.3% and +1.9%; the stock is already down 19% since July and two months of silence (item 1) argue against a fresh warning.

basis: Items 0 and 1: the release lands around 19:00 CET, after the close, so the scored bmo window holds no print, and board-day sessions have a median move of 0.00%.
against: A leak or an early release would put the clinical or NFP headline (items 2-3) inside the window, but its direction is unknown.

basis: Items 0 and 1: four-month sales were down 20% and the H2 bridge needed to hold broker FY26 revenue is steep, while the board halved its own EPS-CAGR vesting hurdle the day after reaffirming; item 2 adds a 23.6% buyback-supported rally into the print, on a name whose interims and outlook prints have fallen double digits.
against: The AGM statement said April-May was ahead year on year, the soft 2025 comparative is real, and a Barry M bargain-purchase gain (item 3) or a guide-holding outlook could squeeze a thin float.

basis: Items 0 and 3: the weak H1 implied by the bitcoin drawdown is offset by a 35% recovery since the period end and a buyback authority vote the next day.
against: The event date and base rate are both unverified (cadence implausible), and the H1 weakness is inferable from public bitcoin prices.

basis: Items 0 and 1: the bid-price compliance deadline expires on the print day, a reverse-split commitment is likely, and an adjudicated default liability must be measured in the FY accounts.
against: A second 180-day period is available (item 3), the Rizobacter debt improvement (item 2) cuts the other way, and a $0.43 distressed stub already prices most of this.

basis: Items 0 and 2: the Remexian put remeasurement and free cash flow sit below the three metrics already pre-announced, and item 1 (German regulatory delay) offsets them.
against: The quarter was pre-announced, so the remeasurement is a below-the-line item the market typically looks through; nothing here has a clear sign.

basis: Items 0, 2 and 3: record summer heat, covenant headroom that removes the credit tail, and post-quarter officer grants tied to positive H2 comps, all against a stock at its 52-week low with downside skew bid.
against: Item 1, the World Cup drag Lucky Strike reported for the same weeks, could make the quarter and the new CEO's outlook worse than -4%, and 13 straight negative comp quarters is the base rate.

basis: Item 0: 8% short interest and a placement 17.5% underwater into a low-information financial print after resolved overhangs; items 1-2 are small negatives.
against: Financial prints barely move this clinical-stage name, call skew already prices the upside, and the EMA omission or the pre-deal cash optics could weigh on it.

basis: Items 1 and 0: HNI's primary release shows contract orders accelerating inside MLKN's fiscal Q1 against easy comparisons, and an IEEPA refund (peer RH booked $55m) is unrecognised and unmodelled, into a 12% 20-day de-rating.
against: The guide is the line that moves this stock; a new CEO search, a thin goodwill cushion (item 2) and a backlog down 10.8% could produce a cautious outlook, as the -22% March print showed.

basis: Items 0 and 1 (pre-announced comps above the stale consensus, 25% of float short) point up; item 2 (a new CEO's first FY27 guide with a value-platform margin drag) points down and is the line that decides the day.
against: Whichever way the FY27 EBITDA guide lands decides it, and the evidence does not settle which side of the $181m consensus that is.

basis: Item 3: the standing FY guide needs a back-loaded Q4 at about 17-18% gross margin while Lennar guided its same quarter flat at 15.5-16%, so a guide trim is likely; item 4 adds a CFO vacancy.
against: Items 0-2 (community growth, lower cancellations, peers' sequential margin gains) plus 12.9% short and call skew make an upside squeeze plausible, as in June's +16.65%.

basis: Items 0 and 1: the +8.7% five-day run-up rests on a rename the 8-K says changes nothing, the data-centre business is about 4% of the quarter, and steel at a four-year high hit a converter that missed on margins last print; the stock has fallen on each of its last four earnings releases.
against: WAVE JV earnings are improving (item 2, about 40% of earnings), consensus has already been cut 5%, and investor-day anticipation may keep holders in through the print.

basis: No item was filed; Radiant exposure, the IB fee proxies and the AM consensus were all checked and found priced or mixed (items 1-5).
against: A quantified Point Bonita/Radiant loss in the release could move the stock either way, and the evidence does not size it.

basis: Item 0 (a Q4 revenue beat likely against a guide-midpoint consensus) is offset by item 2 (an FY27 guide carrying three disclosed headwinds).
against: Revenue beats have not paid on this name and the guide line carries the downside tail; with no options market and no history base rate the scale is unclear.

basis: Items 0 and 1: opex run-rate points to about -$0.06 against a -$0.04 bar, and management's stated reluctance to sell inventory in flat prices makes a near-zero-revenue quarter against $9M plausible; misses have been sold.
against: The stock is down 26% in 20 days near its 52-week low with call skew bid and 13.8% short; habitual misses are known, and a dilution gain on the URC stake could offset.

basis: Item 0: an unexplained 17% five-day fall into the print with 18% of float short, so a held guide has a covering mechanism.
against: Six of the last seven prints fell, often on guide cuts, and an unexplained drawdown is worth close to zero; the sector AI/offshoring narrative could produce another cut.

basis: Items 0 and 1: Chinese press reports lending was suspended at end-June, contradicting the H2 profitability line, and the RMB3.4bn unprovisioned affiliate receivable after the auditor change and the affiliate's redemption halt risks a quantified write-down in a late release.
against: At 0.07x book and below net cash, distress is largely priced; the lending-halt claim is single-source and second-hand, and past print reactions have been small.

basis: Item 0 (a quarter pre-announced at or above the high end, against a stale consensus) and item 2 (11.9% short) point up; item 1 (Domo RPO shrinking ahead of the first Domo-inclusive guide) points down.
against: The guide decides the sign on this name, and a Domo-diluted organic ARR bridge could read as negative even if headline revenue guidance rises.
